subject: confidence interval of total abundance in unmarked

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: confidence interval of total abundance in unmarked
parts:
Hi all,

I am using unmarked R package, N-mixture models in particular (function
pcount). As I see the ?pcount help page, total abundance can be easily
reported:

m1 <- pcount(...)
m1r <- ranef(m1)
cat("Modelled abundance: \n")
sum(bup(m1r))

But is it also possible to report its confidence interval?
I know I can get confidence intervals for abundance at separate sites using confint:

confint(m1r, level=0.95)

but this cannot be easily used for the confidence intervals of the total
abundance, since quantile of sum is not necessarily sum of quantiles :-)
(see http://stats.stackexchange.com/q/134976)

So is there any other solution in unmarked?

Thanks,

Tomas

messages.author: 0216939e087e502c
messages.subject: RE: confidence interval of total abundance in unmarked
parts:
Dear Tomas,


you can bootstrap the variance of that derived quantity. For this, you will have to write a function that computes the sum either of the BUPs (from ranef()) or else of the predicted abundances (from predict()) for the set of sites you want to consider. Then, you use parboot() to produce a parametric bootstrap sample of that population total.


Kind regards  --  Marc
